inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: inference-pool-usw — multiple nodes flapping NotReady (3/12 nodes) and increased 502s. Alert rule: infra.k8s.node.probe.failures > 3 in 2m. See metrics: https://monitoring.redwood.example/incidents/2923456789

micah: I'm oncall, looking now. Paging SRE.

micah: quick ask — can someone paste `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-usw -o wide`?

deploy-bot: metric snapshot: errors(5m): +5.2% 502s, p95 latency 800ms (baseline 120ms), affected services: chat-streaming-prod, embed-batch-1. Node status: node-usw-07, node-usw-09, node-usw-12 in NotReady intermittently.

sara: I pulled kubelet logs from node-usw-09, seeing repeated oom_kill messages and kubelet restart loop. snippet:```
Feb 14 13:02:21 node-usw-09 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 24321 (kubelet) score 951 or sacrifice child
Feb 14 13:02:22 node-usw-09 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
Feb 14 13:02:23 node-usw-09 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Failed with result 'signal'.
```

devon: ugh. We had the kubelet memory-backport enabled in the last infra push (kubelet 1.28.2+). Could be an eviction threshold miscalc + local kubelet memory leak. Also check nvidia driver logs for CUDA errors.

tony: I'm going to cordon node-usw-09 and drain it one at a time. Command I'll run:```
kubectl cordon node-usw-09
kubectl drain node-usw-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

micah: do not drain more than one at a time for the pool — we need to retain concurrency for tail latency. If pods don't reschedule fast enough, we'll route lower-priority traffic to dedicated fallback.

tony: restarted kubelet on node-usw-09 via `systemctl restart kubelet` — kubelet came up but we see:```
I0214 13:04:01 kubelet.go:... kubelet: failed to read gpu metrics: cudaErrorUnknown (700)
E0214 13:04:02 runtime: GPU driver reported device lost, resetting context
```

devon: cudaError 700 often means device-side assert or driver hang. Can you check `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` and dmesg for GPU resets? Also paste container logs for the model-serving container if possible.

tony: grabbing dmesg, saw repeated `NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:01:00: GPU has fallen off the bus` events near the times of kubelet restarts. Looks like driver instability after recent kernel/driver combo on that node.

marie: customer-ops: chat-streaming-prod reports spikes in user-facing errors (~20% of requests during 13:02-13:08). We're opening an incident page and notifying top 10 customers on the impacted list.

micah: mitigation plan executed so far: cordoned/drained node-usw-09, restarted kubelet on node-usw-09, cordon node-usw-12 next and reprovision if driver unstable. Also spun up +2 instances in dedicated-usw-small to absorb traffic. Fallback: routing non-enterprise traffic to quantized-model-v2 (lower memory).

devon: rolling a quick change to runtime routing: set modelFallbackPolicy to `prefer-quantized` for low-priority routes. Command:```
redwoodctl routing update --pool inference-usw --fallback quantized-model-v2 --scope low-priority
```

sara: monitoring shows partial recovery: Ready nodes 9/12, error rate dropped to ~1.2%, p95 down to 160ms. Still seeing occasional spikes when a node flaps.

tony: I triggered a replace on node-usw-12 (cordon -> drain -> delete -> replace). New node provisioned with older driver (the known-good release) and joined Ready.

micah: good. For root cause hypothesis: recent infra push upgraded kernel+NVIDIA driver; combined with kubelet memory tweak caused higher OOM pressure and driver instability. Need postmortem to confirm.

marie: FYI we messaged affected customers and offered mitigation steps. No enterprise SLAs breached yet but continuing close watch.

micah: Handoff in 30m to @sara. Current status: degraded -> partial-service restored. Key actions for next oncall: 1) validate all nodes on same driver version or roll back, 2) run kubelet memory eviction tuning audit, 3) run full node reprovision for any node showing GPU fall-off.

sara: Copy, taking over. I'll start the driver-compatibility sweep and coordinate with infra for a controlled rollback if needed. Will run the post-incident checklist and tag runtime + infra for full RCA. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: Incident 2923456789 updated: responder(s) assigned: micah, sara, devon, tony. Severity: elevated to P1 while GPU instability ongoing.

micah: Handoff note (to include in timeline): root cause suspected: driver+kernel incompatibility causing GPU resets + kubelet memory pressure after recent infra push. Immediate mitigations: node cordon/drain + restart, replace unstable nodes, scale up dedicated small pool, fallback to quantized model. Next steps: postmortem, revert or pin driver, kubelet parameter audit. Linking runbook: https://playbooks.redwood.example/node-flap-runbook

sara: taking the alert. I'll update this thread with final state and timeline once stable.

micah: thanks team, logging everything in the incident page and closing my oncall shift. :white_check_mark:
